tom: Hi all, day 2 here. Using Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04) on a Surface Pro. I installed asdf for nodejs/python/go and synced dotfiles from the repo. Two weird things: 1) VS Code integrated terminal sometimes launches PowerShell and sources my Windows profile, which injects aliases that break `npm run start` inside the container; 2) when I try to push to GitHub from WSL, GCM (Git Credential Manager) on Windows prompts a GUI auth but the WSL-side git falls back to password prompt -> fails. Anyone run into cross-boundary credential/tooling issues?
ivy: Welcome Tom! For the VS Code terminal, go to the terminal dropdown and choose the WSL distro ("WSL: Ubuntu"). If the terminal still starts PowerShell, check your VS Code defaultProfile setting. Also add a guard in your Windows PowerShell profile so it doesn't run heavy interactive stuff when the TERM indicates VS Code or non-interactive: `if ($env:TERM -like '*vscode*') { return }`.
tom: I was using "Reopen in Container" and I thought that would pick the WSL shell but it sometimes remembered PowerShell. Changing defaultProfile worked. Thanks.
kevin: For git creds, GCM on Windows doesn't automatically work inside WSL unless you install the WSL helper. Try `sudo apt install git-credential-manager-core` in WSL and then `git-credential-manager-core configure` so WSL git uses the same credential flow. Alternately you can enable the Windows GCM helper by mounting the helper socket: `git config --global credential.helper "/mnt/c/Program\ Files/Git/mingw64/libexec/git-core/git-credential-manager-core.exe"` but that's flaky. We generally prefer installing the Linux GCM inside the distro.
tom: I installed `git-credential-manager-core` in WSL and ran `git-credential-manager-core configure`. After that, `git push` opened the browser auth flow from WSL and succeeded. Good improvement.
ivy: One more wrinkle: if you forward SSH agent from Windows (Pageant) into WSL via `wsl-ssh-pageant`, the GCM flow may prefer SSH vs HTTPS depending on remote URL. Check `git remote -v`. We standardize on SSH for dev clones to avoid credential GUI popups during CI.
kevin: Also watch out for dotfiles mounting into containers. You mentioned syncing repo dotfiles: if you bind your full `~/.dotfiles` into a container it can overwrite distro user configs. Use a `.container` subset or guard interactive code with `if [ -n "$PS1" ]` or `if [[ $- == *i* ]]` in bash/zsh. That prevents entrypoint scripts from hitting aliased commands.
tom: Oh that explains an entrypoint failure I saw earlier (`ll` alias ran in an init script). I removed some interactive bits and now container starts cleanly.
alex: Another small pro tip: for Windows+WSL, prefer asdf installed in the WSL home (not on the Windows FS) so shims are on a native FS for performance. And add `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` to `~/.profile` so GUI apps (and VS Code server) pick it up.
tom: I moved asdf into WSL home and updated PATH in ~/.profile. Also installed the Linux GCM. Everything seems stable now. One leftover: the VS Code Git extension still popped a Windows credential dialog once. Any idea?
kevin: VS Code desktop on Windows sometimes proxies git operations through the Windows host. Use the Remote - WSL extension and open the folder in WSL to ensure the server-side git is used. In Settings set `git.useEditorAsCommitInput` and ensure `git.path` points to the WSL git if needed.
tom: That did it. Thanks for the quick help!
infra-bot: Created ticket IT-5421: "Onboarding note: WSL+GCM guidance + guard interactive dotfiles for containers" assigned to kevin.
tom: I'll add a small checklist item to my onboarding PR covering: install linux-gcm in WSL, move asdf to WSL home, and avoid mounting interactive dotfiles into containers. Appreciate the help :party_parrot:
